evals.name: unstyled-first-run
evals.prompt: A new Cratis Components 4 app renders every control unstyled and no toast ever shows. Give the exact index.css and the provider setup that fix it, and explain the ordering. Code in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: index.css imports @cratis/components/tokens first, then styles, then optionally theme, imported from the entry with import './index.css'. CratisComponentsProvider from the package root wraps the tree with locale and toaster so toasts show; mount exactly one toaster. Provider carries no theme.
assertions: Imports @cratis/components/tokens before @cratis/components/styles, with theme optional and last.
Mounts CratisComponentsProvider imported from the package root @cratis/components above the app.
Enables the toaster through the toaster prop on the provider and says to mount only one toaster, not both the provider's and a standalone one.
States the provider carries locale and messages but no theme.

evals.name: dark-mode-and-overrides
evals.prompt: We import the baseline theme. Dark mode must follow a user toggle, and our `:root { --cratis-surface-ground: #fafafa }` override is ignored when dark. Show how to toggle dark mode and how to fix the override. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Toggle with document.documentElement.classList.toggle('cratis-dark', darkMode); no provider option. A plain :root rule after theme loses to dark selectors like :root.cratis-dark, so match the scheme selector specificity and place overrides after the import, or omit theme and use a product theme. Use token not hard-coded hex for chrome.
assertions: Toggles dark mode by adding or removing the cratis-dark class on the root element, not via a provider option.
Explains a plain :root override loses to dark selectors such as :root.cratis-dark.
Fixes it by matching the scheme selectors' specificity and placing overrides after the theme import, or by omitting theme.
Does not suggest hard-coding a hex value in component styles for UI chrome.

evals.name: pt-wrong-surface
evals.prompt: Our `pt` on DataPage and on StepperCommandDialog changes nothing visible. Explain which prop targets which surface for DataPage, StepperCommandDialog and Column filters, and how to find the right part name for a selector. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: DataPage: tablePt (DataTableParts), paginatorPt (TablePaginatorParts), menubarPt (ButtonParts). StepperCommandDialog: pt is the inner stepper, dialogPt the outer dialog. Column: filterPt for the filter popup. Read data-cratis-part off the rendered element or the parts manifest because the Toolbar family prefixes names; ptOptions and unstyled do nothing; there is no global provider pt.
assertions: Names tablePt, paginatorPt and menubarPt as the DataPage surface props.
Says StepperCommandDialog pt targets the inner stepper and dialogPt the outer dialog.
Names filterPt for a Column filter popup.
Says to read the data-cratis-part value from the rendered element rather than guessing, and not to target React Aria class names.

evals.name: migration-leftovers
evals.prompt: Migrating from Components 3: the provider has license, theme, unstyled and ptOptions, and package.json still lists primereact and primeicons. What should we do with each? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Components 4 has no Prime dependency; remove leftover Prime packages unless the app itself imports them directly (then that island owns its provider, theme and license). The Components 3 renderer keys (license, theme, defaults, global pt, ptOptions, ripple, unstyled, z-index) are type errors on purpose; theming is CSS via tokens/theme; ptOptions/unstyled as pt props are no-ops.
assertions: Says Components 4 declares no PrimeReact or PrimeIcons dependency and leftover Prime packages should be removed unless the application imports them directly.
Says the old provider keys such as license, theme and unstyled are type errors on purpose.
Says theming is done with CSS: the tokens, styles and optional theme stylesheet entries and --cratis-* custom properties.
Says ptOptions and unstyled do nothing.

evals.name: tailwind-layers
evals.prompt: Our app uses Tailwind and component rules beat our utilities while `pt` classes lose. We declared the layer order after the imports. What is wrong and what exactly should we do? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Tailwind is one supported way to write the CSS, not the default; styles ships no Preflight. The host must put the layer order in its first @layer statement parsed before any stylesheet (e.g. inline style), naming properties, theme, base, cratis-theme, cratis-components, cratis-utilities, components, utilities; declaring after imports cannot reorder established layers.
assertions: Says declaring the layer order after the imports cannot reorder layers already established.
Says the layer-order statement must be the first @layer statement parsed, before any stylesheet, for example an inline style in the host.
Includes the cratis-theme, cratis-components and cratis-utilities layers above the product's components and utilities layers.
Says Cratis internal utilities are prefixed cratis: and are not public styling hooks.
